name: Avions Voisin C25 Aerodyne
description:
One of the most extraordinary and avant-garde automobiles of the 1930s, the Avions Voisin C25 Aérodyne represents the unique vision of Gabriel Voisin, an aviation pioneer who brought aircraft engineering principles to automotive design.

Built between 1934-1937, the C25 Aérodyne featured revolutionary streamlined bodywork designed with aerodynamic efficiency in mind, a rare consideration in its era. The distinctive Art Deco styling, with its flowing lines and integrated fenders, made it one of the most visually striking cars of the decade.

Powered by a refined 3.0-liter Knight sleeve-valve straight-six engine producing 105 horsepower at 3800 RPM, the C25 prioritized smoothness and silence over outright performance. The sleeve-valve design, borrowed from aviation technology, ran whisper-quiet and delivered its power with exceptional refinement - a hallmark of Voisin engineering.

The lightweight aluminum construction (1150 kg) and aerodynamic body allowed for respectable performance despite the modest power output. This was a car built for the discerning connoisseur who valued innovation, elegance, and engineering artistry above conventional luxury.

Today, the Avions Voisin C25 Aérodyne remains a celebrated example of French automotive exceptionalism and one of the most collectible pre-war automobiles.
